While Orestes flees, Apollo appears again and drives the Erinyes out of his temple. A first conflict between the contending deities is presented here, as it were a prelude to the one in Athens; thus partly to prepare for this, partly to gloss over the long time of Orestes' flight, which could not be done here by a choral ode. The young god behaves hostilely and imperiously (like a young lord, as has been said), the old goddesses with dignity and restraint, as also later; from 213 onward, however, Apollo's tone is equally dignified.
